clue.text: Cold sore

definitions.meaning: a biting, freezing wind is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an icy wind can be called this, and so can a person nursing a grudge.

clue.text: See 24
Message to take down, quickly read out?

indicators.note: saying the words aloud at speed slurs them together into one syllable-pair, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: to take food down is to eat it, giving the phrase 'to eat'

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a note to be jotted down and then read back in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To take down' looks like dictation, but it means swallowing: 'to eat', gabbled fast, runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A post on the social platform formerly called Twitter is the familiar name for a short online message.

clue.text: Fuel compared to first of oil in middle of well

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside the other here
middle of keeps the word well without its outer letters

parts.note: 'than' is the word used when comparing one thing to another

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word oil

explanation.surface: A comparison of fuels drawn from the centre of an oil well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of well' here means the word with its outer letters stripped off, not a mid-point letter; 'compared to' supplies the comparison word.
explanation.definitionFit: This alcohol is blended into petrol and burnt as a biofuel, so it is a type of fuel.

clue.text: See 10
Mysterious vessel in time capsized

indicators.note: in puts the container word inside the other
a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the word era is turned over

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a can is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: A strange container buried in a time capsule has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' acts only on the word for time, so the vessel stays the right way round when it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arcane is secret or obscure, understood only by a few, hence mysterious.

clue.text: Tongue in pain ultimately, doctor operates to sew it up

indicators.note: sewing up encloses the final letter of pain within the rearranged letters
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of operates are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of the word pain

explanation.surface: A surgeon operates on a painful tongue and stitches the wound closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges OPERATES, and 'to sew it up' encloses N, the last letter of pain, inside that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, and this is the constructed international language devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: Overly sweet claret drunk with last of sherry

indicators.note: drunk suggests being messed up and unsteady, so the letters of claret are jumbled
last of takes the final letter of the word sherry

explanation.surface: Claret drunk alongside sherry would taste cloyingly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Like molasses syrup, something described this way is sickly and cloying, figuratively over-sentimental.

clue.text: Combination of painful and exciting strokes? That's it!

definitions.text: Combination of painful and exciting strokes? That's it!

parts.words: Combination of painful and exciting strokes? That's it!
parts.note: a smack hurts and a light stroking excites; joined together they name jokey British slang for amorous horseplay, with 'it' the usual euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Someone describes a mix of painful and thrilling strokes and declares that is exactly it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is old-fashioned British slang for playful sexual activity, combining a smack with gentle stroking.

clue.text: Weasel's relative staff and I put back in absurdly long hole?

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round letters inside the golf hole

parts.note: a golf hole is rated par three to five; a 'par ten' would be ridiculously long

indicators.note: put back means the words staff and I are written in reverse order

parts.note: a firm's staff are its men, its workers

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a weasel's cousin hiding in a strangely long burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole' is a golf hole: PAR TEN. 'put back' turns MEN and I into INEM, which goes in after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree-dwelling animal belongs to the mustelid family, the same family as the weasel, stoat and otter.

clue.text: Egg beater father damaged — might he be coddling?

parts.note: an eggbeater is old slang for a rotary-winged aircraft, from the whirling blades
pa is an informal word for father
rent means torn, ripped, hence damaged

explanation.surface: An egg whisk broken by Dad, with a nod to coddled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg beater' and 'coddling' make an egg-cooking scene, but the beater is aircraft slang and coddling is overprotecting a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a mother or father who hovers over a child, overprotecting and pampering it.

clue.text: See 9
Tiny spot that's pink on leg

indicators.note: on means the word for pink sits next to the word for leg

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so one leg is a pin
to pink is to pierce lightly or nick, as in pinking with a sword

explanation.surface: A small pink mark appears on someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' looks like a colour, but here it is the verb meaning to stab lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute hole or dot, like one made with a needle point, is a tiny spot.

clue.text: Drug that's popular filling plate beside me

indicators.note: beside places the word me next to the rest
filling means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a scale is a thin plate, like those on a fish or armour
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Someone sees a popular drug piled onto a plate right next to them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hallucinogenic alkaloid taken from the peyote cactus, a psychedelic substance.

clue.text: Bodily hole in shade of pink

indicators.note: in puts the word for hole within the colour

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange shade
a pore is a tiny hole in the skin

explanation.surface: A hole appears in something coloured pink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having a physical, material body rather than a spiritual one.

clue.text: Old strip with hat in yellow and pink, primarily

parts.note: with means 'and', joining one thing to another

indicators.note: in sets the hat between those two letters
primarily takes the first letters of yellow and pink

parts.note: a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: Describing an old comic strip whose character wears a hat in yellow and pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The British comic strip's hero, a work-shy northerner, always wears a flat cap, so the hat belongs in the picture too.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British newspaper cartoon strip, begun in 1957 in the Daily Mirror, so a strip of old.

clue.text: Three quarters of twelve people on a Hebridean isle

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word keeps three letters, dropping the last

parts.note: a jury in a trial is made up of twelve people

explanation.surface: Nine of a dozen people end up on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: An island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its whisky and red deer.

clue.text: Pace jerk has wrong, upped

parts.note: to jog is to jolt or nudge, a jerk

indicators.note: in a down clue, upped means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A rhythm that a fool got wrong and then quickened.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a steady, easy running gait, a slow measured pace.

clue.text: Game, one prodding virile chap?

parts.note: a stud is a sexually virile man
something or someone that prods or jabs is a poker

explanation.surface: A cheeky game in which someone prods a macho man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a form of the card game in which some cards are dealt face up, a casino gambling game.

clue.text: Lower temperature necessary in the end above church altarpiece

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the earlier letters on top of the church abbreviation

parts.note: to dip is to lower briefly

indicators.note: in the end picks the last letter of necessary

explanation.surface: Turning down the heat in a church, needed above the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting on two hinged panels, often placed over an altar in a church.

clue.text: Better shears cutting coat of ewe

indicators.note: cutting means the word for shears cuts into those outer letters
the coat of a word is its outer letters, the two Es of ewe

parts.note: shears as a verb means clips, cuts wool

explanation.surface: Better shears for clipping the fleece of a ewe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective about the shears, but it is a verb: to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine or surpass something is to put it in the shade, the way the moon blocks the sun.

clue.text: Drunk was irritated

definitions.meaning: to stew is to fret and fume, so this is the past tense: fumed

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for inebriated, and stewing over something means brooding in annoyance.

clue.text: One doesn't believe it: number reversed in account

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the account abbreviation
reversed means it and the song word are written backwards together

parts.note: a number is a song, a piece of music

explanation.surface: A sceptic insists a figure must have been mistakenly flipped in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure; IT SONG reversed gives GNOSTI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a person who holds that the existence of God cannot be known, so withholds belief.

clue.text: Wee like wee?

definitions.meaning: wee as an adjective means small, trifling
wee as a noun is urine; something resembling piddle is jokily described with a -y ending

explanation.definitionFit: The word means trivial or paltry, and it also playfully suggests resembling urine, from piddle.

clue.text: Look back in anger after Nov 31, fancifully?

indicators.note: after means the letter from anger follows the date

parts.note: November has only thirty days, so a fanciful 31st would be December 0, written DEC O

indicators.note: back in picks the final letter of the word anger

explanation.surface: John Osborne's play Look Back in Anger is set beside an impossible date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look back in anger' looks like the play title, but 'Look' is the definition and 'back in anger' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: The style and furnishings of a room give it its look, its interior design.

clue.text: Circling oil platform, sustainable power demanded — privileged few going to the country?

definitions.text: privileged few going to the country?

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly, sustainable
British slang 'give it some welly' means put power into it

indicators.note: circling means the word for demanded wraps round the word for the platform

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, so it means ordered, demanded
an oil rig is a drilling platform at sea

explanation.surface: An oil platform, encircled by protesters demanding green power, seen as a privileged clique.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for well-off townies in rubber boots, wellies being Wellington boots, who visit the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase mocks affluent, upper-class people who adopt country pursuits and dress, a privileged rural set.

clue.text: See 15
Reflective poem set in Spanish city

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so poem and set are read backwards together

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a lot is a set, a batch, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A thoughtful poem set in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' seems to describe a pensive poem, but it signals the letters reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the historic former capital of Castile, on the River Tagus, famous for swords and El Greco.

clue.text: Storm damage

definitions.meaning: to storm is to rush at and attack
damage is jokey slang for cost, as in asking what the bill comes to

explanation.definitionFit: Rushing an enemy position is an attack of that name, and a price levied is a fee, the cost.
